subject: Theory of Automata and Formal Languages
syllabusNote: Topic grouping is a study aid; validate against the student's applicable AKTU regulation and syllabus.

theory.question: Explain DFA and NFA and show why both recognize regular languages.
modelAnswerPoints: A DFA has a unique next state per symbol
an NFA may have multiple possibilities
subset construction converts NFA to equivalent DFA.

mcq.question: A DFA has, for each state and symbol,
mcq.explanation: The deterministic transition function selects one state.

theory.question: Explain correspondence between regular expressions and finite automata.
modelAnswerPoints: Thompson construction converts regex to ε-NFA and state elimination goes the other direction.

mcq.question: Which language class do regular expressions describe?
mcq.explanation: Classical regular expressions are equivalent in expressive power to finite automata.

theory.question: Define derivation, parse tree and ambiguity in CFGs.
modelAnswerPoints: A parse tree records derivation structure
ambiguity occurs when one string has two distinct parse trees/leftmost derivations.

mcq.question: A CFG is ambiguous if
options: One string has two distinct parse trees
mcq.explanation: Two parse trees for a string witness ambiguity.

theory.question: Explain why a PDA can recognize some nonregular languages.
modelAnswerPoints: A PDA has a stack, enabling counting/nesting patterns such as balanced parentheses.

mcq.question: What distinguishes a PDA from a finite automaton?
mcq.explanation: A pushdown automaton has stack memory.

theory.question: Describe a Turing machine and distinguish decidable from recognizable languages.
modelAnswerPoints: A TM has finite control, tape and read/write head
deciders halt on every input, recognizers may loop on rejected inputs.

mcq.question: A language is decidable when a TM
options: Halts on all inputs and answers membership
mcq.explanation: Deciders must terminate on every input.
